title: Weil morphisms are exactly normalized etale-fibre intertwiners
statement: Fix a prime $l$, an algebraic closure $Q$ of $\mathbf Q_l$, a connected Noetherian separated scheme $Y$ on which $l$ is invertible, a geometric point $t$, and an automorphism $h:Y\simeq Y$. Use the actual etale lisse algebraic coefficient category and $h^*$ of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves, def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]. Let $G$ be a group with degree datum $d$, and let $D$ identify the geometric fundamental group at $t$ with $\ker d$ and supply the normalized path to $h(t)$ as in [def-wf-fundamental-representation, sk-d-real-weil]. For every two etale lisse Weil sheaves $F,H$, there is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(F,H)$ to the $Q$-linear intertwiners from their prescribed fundamental representation to each other. For every arrow $a$, the linear map of the corresponding intertwiner is exactly the actual etale stalk map of the underlying sheaf arrow at $t$.

proof.text:
the finite evaluation dictionary of cor-galois-lisse-representations, followed
by inverse limits, rationalization and common coefficient extension, identifies
underlying lisse morphisms with geometric intertwiners. Its finite evaluation rule
agrees with etaleFinitePathIso on every finite-cover germ; the limit projections
and pure tensors then identify its geometric action with etaleGeometricRep.
For an underlying morphism a, naturality of the normalized path and of the
pullback-fibre comparison identifies the descent square with the equation
A T_F = T_H A. Conversely this equation and faithfulness of the underlying
dictionary imply the descent square. The degree datum writes every group element
as a geometric element times an integral power of its degree-one lift, so a map
is a Weil intertwiner exactly when it is a geometric intertwiner and satisfies
this single equation. This proves both directions and uniqueness. The resulting
bijection has exactly the displayed underlying linear map, including zero objects
and zero-rank fibres; no invertibility is required of a morphism.
